sources.news_title: Last Hour of the u.s. and Israel War on Iran, Live Trump Says Iran Has Called for a Ceasefire · Global Voices
sources.text:
Última hora de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, en directo | Irán lanza su mayor oleada de misiles contra Israel de las últimas semanas
Trump asegura que Irán ha pedido un alto el fuego y Teherán lo desmiente | El republicano presiona a Europa para que participe en una coalición para reabrir Ormuz con la amenaza de detener el suministro de armas a Ucrania | Un bombardeo en Teherán hiere a un exministro y mata a su mujer
Irán ha lanzado su mayor oleada de misiles contra Israel (en torno a 10) desde los primeros días de la guerra, según el ejército, sin que hayan trascendido datos de víctimas. Mientras, el presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, ha asegurado en su red social Truth que Teherán ha solicitado un alto el fuego. “Lo consideraremos cuando el estrecho de Ormuz esté abierto”, ha afirmado. Unas declaraciones que Irán desmiente: “Son falsas e infundadas”. Por otro lado, Trump ha declarado al diario británico The Telegraph que está considerando sacar a EE UU de la OTAN, tras la negativa de muchos de sus miembros a participar en la campaña contra Teherán. También ha amenazado con detener el suministro de armas a Ucrania para presionar a los europeos a unirse a una coalición para reabrir Ormuz. Horas antes, había asegurado que las tropas estadounidenses se retirarán “en dos o tres semanas”. El mandatario se dirigirá este miércoles por la noche a los estadounidenses en un discurso televisado. Por su parte, el primer ministro británico, Keir Starmer, ha anunciado una cumbre internacional para debatir sobre la reapertura de Ormuz. Sobre el terreno, un ataque contra Teherán ha herido al exministro de Exteriores Kamal Jarazi y matado a su esposa, según la agencia de noticias iraní Mehr.
EL PAÍS ofrece de forma gratuita la última hora del ataque de EE UU e Israel contra Irán. Si quieres apoyar nuestro periodismo, suscríbete.
Suben los precios de los combustibles en Emiratos Árabes Unidos
Por Izadora Del Bianco. Los nuevos precios de los combustibles han entrado en vigor este miércoles en Emiratos Árabes Unidos, según han informado medios locales tras el anuncio del Comité de Precios de Combustible. La gasolina Super 98 pasa a costar 3,39 dirhams por litro (unos 0,85 euros), frente a los 2,59 dirhams (0,65 euros) de marzo. La Special 95 se sitúa en 3,28 dirhams por litro (alrededor de 0,82 euros), frente a 2,48 dirhams (0,62 euros) el mes anterior, mientras que la E-Plus sube a 3,20 dirhams (unos 0,80 euros), desde los 2,40 dirhams (0,60 euros) previos. El diésel registra el mayor incremento. Alcanza los 4,69 dirhams por litro (aproximadamente 1,18 euros), frente a los 2,72 dirhams (0,68 euros) del mes pasado.
Pezeshkian dirige una carta al pueblo estadounidense: la guerra “es producto de los caprichos económicos de los poderosos”
El presidente iraní, Masud Pezeshkian, ha publicado una carta en la red social X dirigida “al pueblo de Estados Unidos de América”, en la que plantea que el Gobierno de Donald Trump no está actuando en defensa de los intereses de los estadounidenses sino “influenciado y manipulado” por Israel. Pezeshkian, que denuncia una campaña de desinformación sobre su país, pide a los estadounidenses que se pregunten: “¿Es ‘América First’ realmente una de las prioridades del Gobierno de Estados Unidos hoy?”.
Tras asegurar que Irán nunca inició una guerra y, en el actual conflicto, “buscó un acuerdo y cumplió sus compromisos”, niega que su país constituya una amenaza: “Presentar a Irán como una amenaza solo es producto de los caprichos políticos y económicos de los poderosos, de la necesidad de fabricar un enemigo para justificar la presión, mantener la dominación militar, sostener la industria armamentística y controlar mercados estratégicos”. El presidente iraní justifica además que Irán ha intentado mejorar sus capacidades defensivas en “legítima defensa” ante la concentración de fuerzas y bases por parte de Estados Unidos a su alrededor.
En la carta, el dirigente de la república islámica insiste en que el pueblo iraní “no alberga enemistad hacia otras naciones, incluyendo al pueblo de Estados Unidos, Europa o los países vecinos”. Se muestra especialmente crítico con Israel, al que acusa de intentar desviar la atención de sus crímenes contra los palestinos y de usar “hasta el último soldado estadounidense y el último dólar del contribuyente estadounidense para sus intereses ilegítimos”. En cualquier caso, advierte: A lo largo de milenios de orgullosa historia, Irán ha sobrevivido a muchos agresores. Todo lo que queda de ellos son nombres empañados en la historia, mientras Irán perdura resiliente, digno y orgulloso”. (Efe)
Herido un exministro de Exteriores de Irán en un bombardeo contra Teherán en el que ha muerto su esposa
El exministro de Exteriores de Irán Kamal Jarazi ha resultado herido en un bombardeo contra una zona residencial de Teherán en el que ha muerto su esposa, según la agencia de noticias iraní Mehr. Hasta el momento, las autoridades no han hecho declaraciones al respecto.
El diplomático de 82 años ejerció como ministro de Exteriores durante casi una década, desde 1997 hasta 2005, y en los últimos años fue estrecho asesor del fallecido líder supremo de Irán, el ayatolá Alí Jamenei, muerto en la primera jornada de ataques de Estados Unidos e Israel contra territorio iraní el pasado 28 de marzo. (EP)
Trump amenaza con detener el suministro de armas a Ucrania para presionar a los europeos a unirse a una coalición para reabrir Ormuz
El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha amenazado con detener el suministro de armas a Ucrania para presionar a los aliados europeos a unirse a una coalición para reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz, ha publicado el Financial Times el miércoles, citando a personas cercanas a las negociaciones. Según estas fuentes, Trump ha amenazado con parar los suministros a la iniciativa de adquisición de armas de la OTAN para Ucrania financiada por países europeos. (Reuters)
Pezeshkian publicará un escrito dirigido a los estadounidenses en horas
Un funcionario iraní ha anunciado que el presidente de Irán, Masud Pezeshkian, publicará una “importante carta” dirigida a los estadounidenses en unas horas. (Reuters)
Irán anuncia más ataques contra Israel a un minuto de que comience el plazo que se fijó para atacar empresas de EE UU
El jefe de la Fuerza Espacial de la Guardia Revolucionaria, Majid Musavi, ha anunciado otro ataque contra Israel y otros países de la región. El comunicado ha llegado un minuto antes de que empezara el plazo que se ha dado Teherán para atacar empresas estadounidenses como Apple y Google en Oriente Próximo. “Preparen sus refugios”, ha escrito en la red social X en persa, árabe y hebreo Musavi, responsable del programa de misiles iraní.
El militar ha publicado el mensaje a las 19.59 hora local (18.29 en la España peninsular), un minuto antes de la hora en la que Irán anunció ayer que hoy comenzarían los ataques contra 18 empresas tecnológicas y militares estadounidenses en la región. En esa lista de empresas, se encuentran Microsoft, Apple y Google, HP, Intel, Meta, IBM y Boeing, entre otras. (Efe)
Irán lanza su mayor salva de misiles contra Israel de las últimas semanas
Irán acaba de lanzar su mayor oleada de misiles contra Israel (en torno a 10) desde los primeros días de la guerra, según datos preliminares del ejército. Lo ha hecho justo a punto de comenzar la festividad de Pesaj, la Pascua judía. De momento no se ha informado de víctimas.
Ascienden a 1.318 los muertos en Líbano
El balance de muertos por los ataques israelíes contra Líbano asciende a 1.318, mientras que el número de heridos se eleva a 3.935, según ha informado el Centro de Operaciones de Emergencias libanés.
De acuerdo con los últimos datos difundidos por la oficina, parte del Ministerio de Salud Pública de Líbano, entre el total de fallecidos hay 125 niños. (Efe)
Irán desmiente las declaraciones de Trump sobre una solicitud de alto el fuego
El portavoz del Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Irán ha dicho que la declaración del presidente de EE UU, Donald Trump, sobre una solicitud de alto el fuego por parte de Irán es “falsa e infundada”, según ha informado la televisión estatal iraní este miércoles. (Reuters)
El ejército israelí mata en Líbano a 50 personas en 24 horas, según Beirut
El ejército israelí ha matado a 50 personas durante las últimas 24 horas de ofensiva sobre Líbano, según el ministerio de Sanidad libanés. El Ministerio añade que la metralla israelí ha causado también 185 heridos desde el martes. El recuento, que Beirut actualiza a diario, incluye entre las últimas víctimas a un trabajador sanitario y a un menor de edad.
Desde el 2 de marzo, cuando Hezbolá interrumpió 15 meses de alto el fuego que había respetado pese a la continuación de los ataques israelíes, la ofensiva israelí ha causado un total de 1318 muertos y casi 4000 heridos. Siempre según el balance del Gobierno, la lista de víctimas incluye 125 niños muertos y más de 400 heridos.
Las tropas israelíes, que han perdido dentro de Líbano a 10 soldados a manos de Hezbolá, golpean el sector de la salud en lo que se percibe como un intento de vaciar la región libanesa fronteriza con Israel, donde el ejército israelí lucha para ampliar la ocupación en el marco de la guerra contra la milicia chií. Según Beirut, la aviación israelí ha matado a 53 trabajadores sanitarios y ha herido a otros 137. Ese balance llega después de que Israel haya bombardeado 67 vehículos sanitarios, 20 centros médicos o ambulatorios y 82 equipos de emergencias, según el ministerio de Sanidad liderado por Rakan Nassereddine, que niega que la infraestructura médica se explote en Líbano para fines militares, tal y como plantea Israel sin aportar pruebas al respecto.
Mensaje de Donald Trump en Truth Social, este miércoles 1 de abril.
Trump asegura que Irán ha pedido un alto el fuego
Irán ha pedido un alto el fuego a Estados Unidos, según ha asegurado el presidente Donald Trump. En un mensaje en redes sociales, el mandatario ha sostenido que “el presidente del nuevo régimen” en la República Islámica, “mucho menos radicalizado y mucho más inteligente que sus predecesores”, “acaba de pedir a Estados Unidos un ALTO EL FUEGO”.
Trump sostiene que Washington se planteará ese alto el fuego “cuando el estrecho de Ormuz esté abierto, libre y despejado. Hasta entonces, ¡bombardearemos Irán hasta hacerlo desaparecer o, como dicen, de vuelta a la Edad de Piedra!”
No está claro a qué representante iraní se refiere Trump con el título “presidente del nuevo régimen”. Tras la muerte en los bombardeos del líder supremo, Alí Jameneí, Teherán designó al hijo del ayatolá, Mojtaba, como su sucesor, aunque Washington nunca le ha reconocido como dirigente. Podría tratarse del presidente del Parlamento, Mohamed Baqer Qalibaf, del que la Administración estadounidense ha apuntado que encabeza las conversaciones que asegura mantener con Teherán sobre el fin de la guerra.
Donald Trump está cada vez más furioso con sus aliados europeos por no unirse a su guerra (y la del israelí Benjamin Netanyahu) contra Irán. El presidente estadounidense, que ha tratado también de que los socios se unan a una operación para forzar la apertura del estrecho de Ormuz, por donde transita el 20% del petróleo mundial, no solo ha vuelto a cargar contra la OTAN, sino que en esta ocasión ha asegurado que se plantea “seriamente” retirar a su país de la Organización del Tratado del Atlántico Norte, creada en 1949 y que desde entonces lidera el país norteamericano. “Nunca me convenció la OTAN. Siempre supe que era un tigre de papel, y el presidente ruso, [Vladímir] Putin, también lo sabe, por cierto”, ha dicho Trump en una entrevista con el periódico conservador británico The Daily Telegraph.
El ministro israelí, Gideon Saar, en una rueda de prensa, el pasado 10 de marzo, en Tel Aviv. / picture alliance / dpa/picture alliance via Getty Images
El Ministro de Asuntos Exteriores israelí: “Hemos eliminado el peligro de aniquilación, pero no podemos prometer que esta sea ‘la última guerra’”
El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores israelí, Giden Saar, ha expresado, un comunicado por las Pascuas judías, que: “Hemos eliminado el peligro de aniquilación. Aún tenemos enemigos amargos y crueles, pero les hemos asestado un golpe severo”, lo cual podría dar pie a una salida del conflicto, pero ha agregado que “no podemos prometer que esta sea ‘la última guerra’” que lleven a cabo contra Irán.
Saar ha indicado que permanecerán “atentos a las tramas de nuestros enemigos”, y que de no haber sido por el accionar de las Fuerzas de Defensa de su país, “Israel habría quedado en una situación imposible”.
Francia recuerda a Trump que la OTAN “no está diseñada para llevar a cabo operaciones en el estrecho de Ormuz”
La viceministra francesa de Defensa, Alice Rufo, ha respondido a las críticas de Donald Trump a la OTAN por no apoyarle en la guerra de Irán recordando que la organización es una alianza diseñada para velar por la seguridad de la zona euroatlántica, no “para llevar a cabo operaciones en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo cual sería una violación de la legalidad internacional”.
Rufo, que regresó el martes de una visita a Líbano para visitar a los cascos azules franceses, se ha hecho eco de las críticas que Trump lleva vertiendo contra la OTAN desde que reclamó a sus aliados que se uniesen a EE UU en una fuerza naval militar para escoltar barcos en el estrecho de Ormuz, con escaso éxito, y tras recibir varias negativas al uso por sus aviones de guerra de bases militares en países europeos. Ha llegado a llamar “cobardes” a los aliados y en un airado mensaje el martes instó a los países perjudicados por el cierre de Ormuz a que aprendiesen a luchar y fueran a por el petróleo por su propia cuenta. Ya este miércoles, ha afirmado que está considerando “seriamente” sacar a EE UU de la OTAN.
“Dejen que les recuerde qué es la OTAN”, ha dicho Rufo. “Es una alianza militar que se ocupa de la seguridad de la región euroatlática. No está diseñada para llevar a cabo operaciones en el estrecho de Ormuz, lo cual sería una violación de la legalidad internacional”, ha dicho la viceministra en una conferencia sobre "Guerra y Paz en París. (Reuters)
Personas paradas cerca un vehículo destruido en un bombardeo israelí en Beirut, Líbano, este miércoles 1 de abril. / Hassan Ammar / AP
Qué ha pasado en las últimas horas
Estas son las principales noticias del día en la guerra en Oriente Próximo a las 14.00 de este miércoles 1 de abril:
- Trump afirma que está pensando "seriamente" en sacar a EE UU de la OTAN. El estadounidense lo está considerando seriamente después de la negativa de muchos de sus miembros a apoyar a EE UU en su campaña contra Irán. Ha afirmado que siempre ha sabido que la Alianza era “un tigre de papel”. El presidente también ha asegurado que su país se retirará “en dos o tres semanas” de la guerra.
- Emiratos Árabes Unidos quiere abrir el estrecho de Ormuz por la fuerza. Diplomáticos de Abu Dabi han pedido a Washington, Europa y distintos países de Asia que formen una coalición militar para permitir el paso por el canal. Los Emiratos también han expresado que la situación “representa una extorsión económica global”.
- Al menos nueve muertos y 24 heridos en los últimos bombardeos israelíes en Beirut. En el marco de la ofensiva israelí contra Líbano desde el inicio de la guerra de Irán el pasado 28 de febrero han muerto ya más de 1.250 personas en Líbano, con 3.750 heridas y más de un millón de desplazados.
- Starmer anuncia una cumbre con líderes europeos para debatir sobre el estrecho de Ormuz. El Primer Ministro ha reiterado que el Reino Unido no se dejará arrastrar a la guerra de Irán y que la mejor forma de contener el impacto de la crisis energética es poner fin al conflicto y reabrir el Estrecho.
El Reino Unido acogerá a finales de esta semana un encuentro con 35 países para buscar el modo de reanudar el tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz, bloqueado por Irán. “La ministra de Exteriores, Yvette Cooper, presidirá un encuentro que reunirá a todas esas naciones por primera vez, para tomar en consideración todas las medidas diplomáticas políticas viables para restaurar la libertad de navegación, garantizar la seguridad de las embarcaciones y tripulaciones atrapadas y resumir el transporte de mercancías vitales”, ha anunciado este miércoles en una rueda de prensa celebrada en Downing Street.
La Armada israelí dice haber matado al comandante del Frente Sur de Hezbolá en un ataque en Beirut
La Armada israelí ha matado en Beirut al comandante del Frente Sur de Hezbolá, identificado por ellos como Hajj Yousef Ismail Hashem, según ha informado este miércoles un comunicado castrense. El ataque tuvo lugar ayer, 31 de marzo, y según el ejército israelí, el Frente Sur es la unidad responsable de preparar ataques así como “operaciones de combate” contra sus soldados en el sur del Líbano; zona que Israel ocupa. Hashem, un alto comandante, asumió el mando de este frente tras el asesinato a manos de Israel de Ali Karaki, junto al líder del grupo Hezbolá, Hasán Nasrala, en septiembre de 2024 en un bombardeo contra los suburbios sur de Beirut, conocidos como el Dahye.
Este miércoles, también en el Líbano, al menos nueve personas murieron y una veintena resultaron heridas en dos ataques del ejército de Israel, uno de ellos contra Beirut. Desde hace casi un mes, el pasado 2 de marzo, Israel mantiene una intensa campaña de bombardeos contra el Líbano acompañada de una operación terrestre, que en conjunto han causado más de 1.200 muertos y de 3.700 heridos, además de más de un millón de desplazados. (Efe)
Francia denuncia una “intimidación inaceptable” del ejército israelí a sus 'cascos azules' en Líbano
El Gobierno francés ha denunciado este miércoles que sus cascos azules destinados en Líbano han sufrido una “intimidación absolutamente inaceptable” por parte del ejército israelí tras los incidentes que costaron la vida a tres soldados indonesios de la misión de Naciones Unidas en Líbano.
Alice Rufo, viceministra de Defensa, ha expresado en París, un día después de regresar de un viaje a Líbano, su “solidaridad con los indonesios”, tras los incidentes del sábado y el domingo en los que murieron tres soldados de esa nacionalidad destinados en la fuerza de paz de la ONU en el país, denominada Finul. Indonesia ha reclamado a la ONU que realice una investigación sobre esos incidentes, cuya responsabilidad no ha sido determinada aún. Israel afirma que es una zona de combate y no sabe aún quién fue el autor de los ataques.
“Quiero enviar un mensaje de solidaridad a nuestros soldados”, ha añadido Rufo, “que han sido objeto de una intimidación completamente inaceptable”, ha dicho en una conferencia en París y después de que fuentes diplomáticas asegurasen que el pasado día 28 se produjeron tes incidentes entre los soldados israelíes y el ejército israelí. (Reuters)
En medio de las confusas declaraciones del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, sobre cómo y cuándo terminar la guerra con Irán que él mismo empezó hace un mes, China y Pakistán han presentado una iniciativa de cinco puntos para “restablecer la paz y la estabilidad” en la región del Golfo y Oriente Próximo.
Jameneí promete “apoyar de manera continua” a Hezbolá contra EE UU e Israel
El líder supremo iraní, Mojtaba Jameneí, ha prometido “apoyar de manera continua [a Hezbolá] en la resistencia contra el enemigo sionista-estadounidense”, en un mensaje publicado en Telegram y difundido por la agencia Tasnim.
Jamení ha respondido así a un mensaje de condolencias que le había extendido el secretario general de Hezbolá, Naim Qassem, a quien el iraní ha celebrado por estar al frente del grupo armado “en este momento crítico e histórico”.
Un hogar destruido durante la actual ofensiva israelí contra Líbano, este miércoles 1 de abril. / Yara Nardi / REUTERS
Ascienden a nueve los muertos en Líbano tras los ataques israelíes
Ascienden a nueve los muertos en Líbano este miércoles en dos ataques del ejército israelí contra diferentes puntos de Líbano, según han informado fuentes oficiales.
"El Centro de Operaciones de Emergencia Sanitaria del Ministerio de Salud Pública emitió un comunicado anunciando que el ataque del enemigo israelí en la zona de Jnah, en Beirut, dejó un saldo final de siete muertos y 26 heridos", de acuerdo a un comunicado reproducido por la Agencia Nacional de Noticias (ANN) libanesa.
De acuerdo con estas mismas fuentes, un segundo ataque aéreo israelí contra un vehículo en Khaldeh, al sur de la capital libanesa, ha causado la muerte de dos personas y ha dejado heridas a otras tres.
Estos ataques tienen lugar en la misma jornada en la que el ejército libanés ha anunciado el "redespliegue y reposicionamiento" de varias de sus unidades en el sur del país como consecuencia de la intensa operación terrestre israelí, que ha provocado el "cerco y aislamiento" de posiciones militares libanesas y la interrupción de sus líneas de suministro. (Efe)
Las interrupciones en el suministro de petróleo desde Oriente Próximo aumentarán en abril y afectarán a Europa
Las interrupciones en el suministro de petróleo desde Oriente Próximo aumentarán en abril, y Europa se verá afectada a medida que los suministros disminuyan debido al cierre del estrecho de Ormuz, según ha expresado este miércoles el director de la Agencia Internacional de Energía (AIE), Fatih Birol.
“La pérdida de petróleo en abril será el doble de la pérdida de marzo, además de la pérdida de gas natural licuado (GNL). El mayor problema hoy es la falta de combustible para aviones y diésel. Estamos viendo eso en Asia, pero pronto, creo, en abril o mayo, llegará a Europa”, ha dicho Birol en un pódcast presentado por Nicolai Tangen, director del fondo soberano de Noruega.
Esta declaración refleja las preocupaciones sobre una posible crisis de suministro, especialmente con respecto a los combustibles críticos para la aviación y el transporte, mientras las tensiones geopolíticas impactan las principales rutas de navegación en la región. (Reuters)
Actualización | Irán lanza cuatro oleadas de misiles contra el centro de Israel
Irán ha lanzado cuatro oleadas de misiles contra la zona centro de Israel en las últimas horas, entre las ocho y once de la mañana hora local del miércoles (las seis y las nueve de la España peninsular), que han causado varios impactos y herido de gravedad a una niña de 11 años.
“Los paramédicos y técnicos de emergencias médicas de la Estrella de David Roja (MDA) están brindando atención médica y evacuando a hospitales a 14 personas, entre ellas: una niña de 11 años en estado grave con heridas de metralla en las extremidades”, ha detallado un portavoz en un comunicado, especificando que fueron trasladadas al Centro Médico Sheba–Tel HaShomer?? (próximo a Tel Aviv).
Entre el total de víctimas registradas esta mañana por los ataques con misiles, algunas de ellas con munición de racimo, hay también una mujer de 36 años y un niño de 13 con heridas por metralla; así como 11 personas heridas leves. Las sirenas por las andanadas de misiles iraníes han sonado hasta en cuatro ocasiones en el centro de Israel, incluyendo el núcleo urbano de Tel Aviv, pero no en Jerusalén, con varios impactos en la zona. (Efe)
Keir starmer, durante su comparecencia de este miércoles en Downing Street. / Frank Augstein / Pool/WPA/Getty
Starmer anuncia una cumbre con líderes europeos para debatir sobre el estrecho de Ormuz
El Reino Unido acogerá a finales de esta semana una cumbre internacional para impulsar la reapertura del estrecho de Ormuz, según ha anunciado el primer ministro británico Keir Starmer durante una rueda de prensa en Downing Street. “La ministra de Extreriores presidirá un encuentro que reunirá a todas esas naciones [35, según ha dicho el primer ministro] por primera vez, para tomar en consideración todas las medidas diplomáticas políticas viables para restaurar la libertad de navegación, garantizar la seguridad de las embarcaciones y tripulaciones atrapadas y resumir el transporte de mercancías vitales”, ha asegurado.
El primer ministro británico ha repetido en varias ocasiones su compromiso de no verse arrastrado al conflicto provocado por Estados Unidos e Israel –“Esta no es nuestra guerra”, ha reiterado- y ha interpretado la amenaza de Donald Trump de abandonar la OTAN, que el presidente estadounidense ha sugerido en una entrevista al diario The Daily Telegraph, como un modo de presionar al Reino Unido y otros aliados para que se impliquen en la ofensiva bélica.
Starmer ha reiterado su voluntad de reforzar la cooperación militar y energética con la UE, y ha anunciado la intención de su Gobierno de reforzar el alineamiento normativo con Bruselas en la próxima cumbre bilaterar que se celebrará antes del verano.
Trump afirma que está pensando "seriamente" en sacar a EE UU de la OTAN
El presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, ha cargado de nuevo contra la OTAN y ha asegurado que está barajando seriamente sacar a EEUU de la Alianza, pese a que hace falta una autorización del senado o una ley del Congreso para hacerlo. El jefe de la Casa Blanca, que está profundamente disgustado con sus aliados europeos por no unirse a la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán ni participar en una operación para abrir el estrecho de Ormuz por la fuerza, ha vuelto a ondear la idea de que el país norteamericano salga de la organización militar que lidera. Así lo ha declarado en una entrevista con el periódico británico Daily Telegraph, en la que describe la Alianza Atlántica, que cuenta con 32 aliados (entre ellos, España, desde 1982) como un “tigre de papel”.
Trump no puede tomar la decisión unilateral de sacar a EEUU de la OTAN. La ley (una regulación promovida por la Administración del demócrata Joe Biden) estadounidense dicta que hace falta una supermayoría de dos tercios del Senado o una ley de Congreso para hacerlo.
Sin embargo, a la pregunta de si reconsideraría la pertenencia de Estados Unidos a la Alianza tras el conflicto, Trump respondió: “Sí, diría que está más allá de la reconsideración”, respondió, dando la idea de que la decisión está prácticamente tomada. “Nunca me convenció la OTAN. Siempre supe que era un tigre de papel, y el presidente ruso, [Vladímir] Putin, también lo sabe, por cierto”, añadió.
Trump tiene previsto dar un discurso este miércoles a las nueve de la noche, de Washington, tres de la madrugada, hora de la España peninsular.
Albares insta a Hezbolá e Israel a cesar sus ataques en el sur de Líbano
El ministro de Asuntos Exteriores, José Manuel Albares, ha denunciado este miércoles que la integridad de Líbano está siendo violentada, su población desplazada, la paz frustrada, y ha instado al grupo chií libanés Hezbolá e Israel a cesar los ataques en el sur del país.
Albares les ha pedido además, en un hilo en las redes sociales, que cumplan la resolución 1701 del Consejo de Seguridad de la ONU que, aprobada por unanimidad en 2006, busca poner fin a las hostilidades entre Hezbolá e Israel.
Asimismo, ha instado a ambas partes a respetar a la Fuerza Provisional de las Naciones Unidas para el Líbano (FPNUL, también conocida como UNFIL, por sus siglas en inglés). (Efe)
Al menos una treintena de ataques en el Kurdistán iraquí
La región del Kurdistán iraquí, en el norte del país, vive una escalada de violencia en los últimos días que esta noche se ha materializado en el lanzamiento de más de 30 ataques con drones sobre distintos puntos, que han causado al menos tres niños heridos.
Además, una empresa británica de aceites para motores fue atacada en la mañana de este miércoles con dos drones iraníes tipo Shahed, de fabricación iraní. El primer impacto ocurrió alrededor de las 7.20 (9.20 en la España peninsular) provocando un incendio masivo en la planta. Aproximadamente una hora después, un segundo dron impactó el mismo lugar, agravando la situación.
Emiratos Árabes Unidos sobre el cierre del estrecho de Ormuz: “Representa una extorsión económica global”
El presidente de la Compañía Nacional de Petróleo de Abu Dabi, Sultan Al Jaber, ha condenado el accionar iraní en el estrecho de Ormuz, y ha expresado que: “No son solo un problema regional, representan una extorsión económica global, una amenaza que el mundo no puede tolerar”.
Sus dichos llegan horas después de que se conociera que los Emiratos Árabes Unidos se están preparando para ayudar a EE UU y sus aliados para reabrir el Estrecho a través de la fuerza. (Reuters).
Israel afirma haber asesinado a un ingeniero de la Guardia Revolucionaria
El ejército israelí ha informado de que en uno de sus ataques del martes sobre Irán, mató a Mahdi Vafaei, un ingeniero de la fuerza Quds, una rama de la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní encargada de las operaciones especiales, que presta apoyo a grupos como Hezbolá, Hamás o los hutíes de Yemen. En concreto, Vafaei era jefe de ingeniería de la división libanesa de la fuerza Quds y falleció en un ataque aéreo ejecutado en Mahallat, a unos 200 kilómetros al sur de Teherán. Irán no ha confirmado la información.
Según el ejército israelí Vafaei fue durante 20 años responsable de “proyectos subterráneos avanzados en Líbano y Siria”, incluyendo “decenas de proyectos subterráneos en Líbano usados para almacenar armamento”. “La eliminación del terrorista Vafaei perjudica la capacidad de producción de infraestructura clandestina de la organización terrorista Hezbolá, así como los esfuerzos del régimen terrorista iraní por promover y ejecutar complots terroristas en todo Oriente Medio”, afirma el ejército israelí en un mensaje en X.

sources.news_title: Breaking: Iran Has Requested a Ceasefire, Trump Says
sources.text:
Breaking: Iran Has Requested a Ceasefire, Trump Says
President Donald Trump says Iran wants a ceasefire, but he is not quite ready to sign a deal.
“Iran’s New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE!” Trump posted Wednesday on Truth Social. “We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear.”
“Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!! President DJT.”
As noted by Axios, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Tuesday said Iran could be willing to stop fighting but the U.S. would need to stop attacking Iran and promise not to attack Iran again.
Trump’s comment comes as U.S. Central Command noted the extent of the pounding Iran has received since the war began on Feb. 11.
“U.S. Navy fighter jets prepare for a combat flight during Operation Epic Fury. To date, U.S. forces have flown over 12,000 combat flights directly supporting Operation Epic Fury,” Central Command posted on X.
On Tuesday night, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said in pre-recorded address that the war has weakened Iran, according to the Jerusalem Post.
“We are heavily crippling the regime that has called for ‘Death to Israel’ and ‘Death to America’ for the past decade,” he said. “The Ayatollah’s regime is weaker than ever and Israel is stronger than ever.”
“Ahead of the war, Israel fought Iran alone. Now, the U.S. and Israel are fighting side by side against Iran.”
Noting Israeli pounding of Hezbollah in Lebanon, Netanyahu added, “we broke the strength of Iran’s proxies that threatened us.”
On Tuesday, Trump indicated the war might be winding down.
“We’re not going to be there too much longer. We’re obliterating… them right now,” Trump told the New York Post.
“We won’t have to be there much longer — but we have more work to do in terms of killing their offensive, whatever offensive capability they have left,” he said.
Trump said the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has blocked during the war will reopen when the fighting ends.
“Well, I think it’ll automatically open, but my attitude is, I’ve obliterated the country. They have no strength left, and let the countries that are using the strait, let them go and open it,” he said. “I would imagine whoever’s controlling the oil will be very happy to open the strait.”

sources.news_title: Donald Trump Conditions Ceasefire in Iran to Open the Strait of Ormuz
sources.text:
Donald Trump aseguró que podría detener los bombardeos contra Irán únicamente si se reabre el Estrecho de Ormuz al libre tránsito.
“¡Acaba de pedir un alto al fuego a los Estados Unidos de América! Lo consideraremos cuando el Estrecho de Ormuz esté abierto, libre y despejado. Hasta entonces ¡Estamos bombardeando a Irán hasta la aniquilación o, como dice, de vuelta a la edad de piedra!”.
Donald Trump, presidente de Estados Unidos.
A través de un mensaje en Truth Social, afirmó que Mojtaba Jamenei le solicitó un alto al fuego, pero condicionó su decisión a la eliminación del pago obligatorio impuesto por Teherán.
De lo contrario, advirtió, la ofensiva militar podría intensificarse hasta la “aniquilación” del país. Irán, por su parte, defendió el cierre del Estrecho de Ormuz como medida de seguridad.
Donald Trump detendrá el fuego contra Irán si abren el Estrecho de Ormuz
Con un post en Truth Social, fue que el presidente de Estados Unidos aseguró que Mojtaba Jamenei, nuevo líder supremo en Irán, le pidió detener el fuego.
Sin embargo, Donald Trump aseguró que podría meditarlo a profundidad solo si Irán decide abrir el Estrecho de Ormuz.
En cambio, si Irán decide no atender la reapertura y libre paso en el Estrecho de Ormuz, Estados Unidos seguirá la “aniquilación” de Irán hasta su exterminio.
Estrecho de Ormuz está abierto, pero bajo el pago obligatorio por transitar
Donald Trump llamó a Irán a reabrir el paso libre en el Estrecho de Ormuz, lo que podría poner un alto al fuego. Sin embargo, ya se puede navegar, pero con un pago obligatorio.
Alaeddin Boroujerdi, miembro de la Comisión de Seguridad Nacional y Política Exterior de Irán, argumentó que el Consejo Consultivo aprobó una nueva normativa sobre el Estrecho de Ormuz que aplica de forma inmediata.
Boroujerdi aseguró que ahora los buques que pasen por el Estrecho de Ormuz deberán dar un pago obligatorio, argumentando la necesidad que Irán tiene para financiar con ello la seguridad a embarcaciones.
Asimismo, se dejó claro que aquellos de Estados Unidos o que colaboren con ellos en bombardeos a Irán, no tendrán paso en el Estrecho de Ormuz.

sources.news_title: President Trump Reveals Iran Has Asked for a CEASEFIRE But This One Condition Must be Met Before He Considers It
sources.text:
The weeks-long war in Iran may be nearing its end, provided the Islamist dictatorship bends the knee on a highly critical condition.
On Wednesday, President Trump took to Truth Social to deliver some promising news: Iran’s new ‘president’ has just asked America for a ceasefire to end the fighting. Trump said he’s considering the proposal but has one condition: that Iran reopen the Hormuz Strait, which the nation closed last month.
Otherwise, the bombing will continue.
The announcement comes just hours before Trump is scheduled to address the country on the war.
“Iran’s New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE!” Trump announced on Truth Social.
“We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear. Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!” he added.
The Hormuz Strait is considered to be one of the world’s most critical oil chokepoints, connecting the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
According to the U.S. Energy Information Administration, it accounts for more than 35% of all seaborne oil trade, largely destined for Asia.
Trump has also provided more reason to believe the bombing campaign will wind down soon during a phone interview with the New York Post on Tuesday.
We’re not going to be there too much longer. We’re obliterating the sh*t out of them right now,” Trump said.
“We won’t have to be there much longer — but we have more work to do in terms of killing their offensive, whatever offensive capability they have left.”
An end to the war will certainly be a welcome relief, especially given that Americans are paying $4 per gallon for gasoline.
High gas prices have a particularly profound impact on working-class people, who make up the majority of Trump’s base.
Getting out of Iran would also likely boost Trump’s poll numbers, which have been in a freefall since the war began.

sources.news_title: Iran ‘Contradicts’ Trump: Rejects Cease-Fire and Warns that Strait of Ormuz ‘Will Not Open up Enemies’
sources.text:
El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, afirmó este miércoles 1 de abril que Irán le solicitó un “alto el fuego” y señaló que considerará esa posibilidad una vez que el estrecho de Ormuz haya sido reabierto.
“El nuevo presidente del régimen iraní, mucho menos radicalizado y mucho más inteligente que sus predecesores, ¡acaba de pedir un alto el fuego a los Estados Unidos de América! Lo consideraremos cuando el estrecho de Ormuz esté abierto, libre y despejado”, aseguró Trump en la plataforma Truth Social, sin especificar a qué líder iraní se refiere.
Hasta entonces, agregó Trump, Estados Unidos sigue “bombardeando a Irán hasta la aniquilación o, como dicen algunos, hasta que regrese a la Edad de Piedra!”.
Sin embargo, la Guardia Revolucionaria Islámica respondió este día que la situación en el estrecho de Ormuz está “firme y dominantemente” bajo su control y “no se abrirá a los enemigos de esta nación por las ridículas demostraciones del presidente de Estados Unidos”.
El líder estadounidense prevé ofrecer un “importante” discurso a la nación a las 21:00 horas de Washington para informar sobre la guerra, en un mensaje que se produce tras una serie de comentarios sobre el posible fin del conflicto.
Trump amenaza con retirar a EU de la OTAN
Trump afirmó este día que prevé “retirarse” de Irán en “dos o tres semanas”, al asegurar que se están logrando los objetivos de la guerra iniciada el 28 de febrero, como evitar que la República Islámica obtenga un arma nuclear.
Tras haber intentado sin éxito liderar una coalición militar con sus aliados para reabrir el estrecho de Ormuz, vía clave para el comercio de crudo que permanece bloqueada por Irán en respuesta a los ataques estadounidenses e israelíes, Trump dijo el martes que este ya no es un asunto de Estados Unidos.
Trump instó a los países de la OTAN y a las naciones asiáticas a actuar con “coraje” y “tomar” el estrecho, por donde circula una quinta parte del petróleo mundial.
En una entrevista publicada este miércoles por el diario británico The Telegraph, Trump dijo que no descarta retirar a Estados Unidos de la OTAN, una organización que definió como un “tigre de papel”.

sources.news_title: In Direct - War in the Middle East: Trump's New Volte-Face, Which Makes the Ceasefire Conditional on the Reopening of the Strait of Ormuz
Trump Says Iran Seeks Ceasefire Deal
sources.text:
President Donald Trump said Iran’s president has sought a ceasefire, but Washington will only consider the request if the Strait of Hormuz is reopened. According to CNBC, the U.S. remains focused on restoring access to the critical oil route before easing military pressure.
The report said it is unclear whether Iran has formally confirmed the ceasefire request or how it was communicated. Questions remain over whether the appeal came directly or through intermediaries such as Pakistan.
US President Donald Trump claims Iran’s president has asked for a ceasefire.

🔴 LIVE updates: https://t.co/NyIs3MwJRw pic.twitter.com/v4We5e3WZx

The month-long war has disrupted global energy markets, with the Strait of Hormuz largely blocked. According to reports, this has driven volatility in oil prices and economic uncertainty worldwide.

sources.news_title: Trump says Iran asked for a ceasefire — but the US has one major condition
sources.text:
Anna Moneymaker/Getty Images

Trump says Iran asked for a ceasefire — but the US has one major condition
April 01, 2026
'We are blasting Iran into oblivion.'
President Donald Trump says Iran's "new regime" has asked the United States for a ceasefire just over a month into the conflict, but the commander in chief still has one major hang-up.
Trump said Wednesday he would consider the ceasefire only if the Strait of Hormuz, which controls about 20% of the world's oil supply, is reopened. This announcement comes the morning of Trump's highly anticipated address to the nation, which is slated to take place at 9:00 pm Eastern Time.
'We will consider when ...'
"Iran's New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE!" Trump said in a Truth Social post Wednesday. "We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear."
"Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!"
RELATED: 'Delayed courage': Trump tells allies to fend for themselves amid oil crisis
Ian Forsyth/Getty Images
This development comes just a day after Trump urged American allies who have been impacted to fend for themselves and get their own oil. He also criticized countries like the United Kingdom and France for their inaction throughout this conflict, saying they will have to "start learning how to fight for [themselves]."
"All of those countries that can't get jet fuel because of the Strait of Hormuz, like the United Kingdom, which refused to get involved in the decapitation of Iran, I have a suggestion for you," Trump said in the Truth Social post Tuesday. "Number 1, buy from the U.S., we have plenty, and Number 2, build up some delayed courage, go to the Strait, and just TAKE IT."

sources.news_title: Trump: Iran Wants Ceasefire Ahead of Prime-Time Speech
sources.text:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday morning said an Iranian request for "a ceasefire" will be considered "when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear."
In a forceful Truth Social post hours before an evening address to the nation, Trump signaled both a willingness to negotiate and a continued hard-line stance against Tehran, tying any potential ceasefire directly to the reopening of the critical global shipping lane.
"Iran's New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE!" Trump wrote.
"We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear. Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!"
The Strait of Hormuz, a vital artery for global energy markets, has been effectively shut down amid the ongoing U.S.-Iran conflict, sending oil prices surging and rattling economies worldwide.
Trump has repeatedly made clear that restoring free passage through the strait is a nonnegotiable priority.
Trump is scheduled to address the nation Wednesday at 9 p.m. ET, offering what the White House described as an "important update on Iran" as the conflict enters a decisive phase.
Officials have suggested the coming days could determine whether the war winds down or escalates further.
According to multiple reports, Trump believes the U.S. has already achieved key military objectives, including significantly degrading Iran's missile capabilities and military infrastructure.
He has said the conflict could end within "two weeks, maybe three," raising the possibility of a swift conclusion if conditions are met.
At the same time, the administration has maintained significant military pressure on Iran.
Hundreds of U.S. Special Operations Forces — including elite Navy SEALs and Army Rangers — have been deployed to the region, alongside Marines and paratroopers, providing Trump with a range of options should negotiations fail.
Department of War officials have reportedly explored potential operations targeting Iran's nuclear assets and oil export infrastructure, including Kharg Island, a key hub for Tehran's energy industry.
Trump has also underscored a broader shift in U.S. policy, signaling that allies who rely on Middle Eastern oil should take greater responsibility for securing their own supply routes.
"All I have to do is leave Iran … and we'll be doing that very soon," Trump said Tuesday, Axios reported, suggesting that U.S. involvement in the region could wind down once objectives are achieved.
Despite Iran publicly denying formal negotiations, officials on both sides have acknowledged indirect communications through intermediaries, fueling speculation that a deal could be within reach.
Still, Trump's latest remarks make clear that any agreement will come on American terms, with the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz serving as a key benchmark.
As energy markets remain volatile and tensions high, Trump's dual-track approach — combining military strength with conditional diplomacy — reflects a strategy aimed at forcing concessions while avoiding a prolonged conflict.
Trump's address Wednesday night is expected to provide further clarity on whether a ceasefire is imminent or whether the U.S. will intensify operations to secure a decisive outcome.

sources.news_title: Trump says Iran's new leader wants ceasefire - but will keep 'blasting' attacks
sources.text:
Donald Trump astonishingly claimed King Charles would have backed the war on Iran and taken a "different stand" from Keir Starmer.
It comes amid conflicting messages between the US and Iran over talks. Iran's foreign ministry dismissed Trump's claim that the country requested a ceasefire as "false and baseless". Meanwhile, new strikes have been reported in both Iran and Israel, and the number of people reported killed in Israeli strikes on Lebanon has surpassed 1,300.
Earlier, Trump said in a Truth Social post: "Iran’s New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE! We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear. Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!! President DJT." It is not clear who Trump is referring to.
Trump's message to Artemis astronauts
Ahead of the Artemis 2 launch, Donald Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social: "We are WINNING, in Space, on Earth, and everywhere in between — Economically, Militarily, and now, BEYOND THE STARS. Nobody comes close!"
He added: "God bless our incredible Astronauts, God bless NASA, and God bless the Greatest Nation ever to exist, the United States of America!"
Reeves to work with supermarket bosses amid fears over food inflation
The Chancellor and supermarket bosses agreed to explore together how to ease the cost of living for consumers amid a warning that the Middle East conflict could see food inflation soar higher than 9% by the end of 2026.
The Food and Drink Federation (FDF), which represents 12,000 food and drink manufacturers, hiked its inflation forecast for the year in light of the conflict.
Rachel Reeves and Energy Secretary Ed Miliband hosted supermarket bosses, including from Tesco, Sainsbury’s and Aldi, for talks at No 11 on Wednesday.
“They agreed to work together to explore what more can be done to ease the cost of living for consumers and strengthen supply chains,” a Government spokesperson said.
Donald Trump suggests King Charles would have backed Iran war
The US president suggested the King would have backed his war in Iran and taken a "different stand" from Keir Starmer.
“I like him. I always liked him as a prince. He’s a good man, a great representative for your country,” Trump told The Telegraph when asked about the King’s upcoming visit the US to mark 250 years of American independence.
He added: “I think he would have taken a very different stand (on the war in Iran), but he doesn’t do that. I mean, he’s a great gentleman.” Trump also said the King was “a friend of mine”, adding that he had “nothing to do with this”, in reference to the breakdown in UK-US relations over the Iran war.
FTSE 100 soars as Middle East peace hopes grow
European stocks rallied on Wednesday as comments from both sides of the Middle East war gave some conviction for a near-term end to hostilities.
“The market appears increasingly optimistic that an end to the war in Iran is in the offing as big gains in the US and Asia were matched in Europe,” said AJ Bell investment director Russ Mould.
The FTSE 100 closed up 188.34 points, 1.9%, at 10,364.79. The FTSE 250 ended up 484.48 points, 2.3%, at 21,688.19, and the AIM All-Share advanced 22.13 points, 3.1%, at 739.25.
On Wednesday, US President Donald Trump said that Iran had asked for a ceasefire but that the US would only consider this once the Strait of Hormuz, the vital oil and gas shipping route which Iran has effectively closed for most exports, is clear for shipping.
This came after Mr Trump told reporters on Tuesday the US would end operations in Iran “very soon”, perhaps within “two weeks, maybe three”.
'I’m angry Trump started Iran war with no plan'
Rachel Reeves has said she is “angry” that Donald Trump launched the Iran war without a “clear plan”, as she warned of economic hardship hitting Britain amid skyrocketing global oil prices.
In the most direct criticism yet from a UK Cabinet minister, the Chancellor hit out at the US president for having “chosen” to start a conflict that “we disagree with”, as Britons brace for a cost-of-living squeeze as a result of the crisis.
She said the war, which Britain did not want to “enter”, would have “implications for our economy”, which were being closely monitored as the government prepares for “every single eventuality”.
Speaking to BBC Radio 2’s Jeremy Vine show on Wednesday, Ms Reeves said: “I think that people can see that what Trump has done in the Middle East is going to cause economic challenges all around the world, with potentially higher inflation, weaker growth and weaker tax receipts.”
'Blasting Iran back to the Stone Ages...'
Trump said Tehran’s new leader has requested a ceasefire, but vowed to continue “blasting Iran back to the Stone Ages” until the critical Strait of Hormuz shipping lane is reopened.
The US president, who is due to make a televised address later on Wednesday, made the announcement in a post on his Truth Social platform.
However, an Iran foreign ministry spokesman called Mr Trump’s comments “false and baseless”.
Mr Trump did not name the regime’s new leader who he said had called for a truce, but said he was “much less radicalised and far more intelligent than his predecessors”.
Iran rejects ceasefire claims
The IRGC says the Strait of Hormuz is “firmly and dominantly” under Iranian control. It added that the Strait “will not be opened to the enemies of this nation by the ridiculous displays of the US President”.
It followed Trump claiming Iran had asked for a ceasefire, which he would consider “when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear”.
Iran Foreign Ministry spokesman also called Trump's remarks on Tehran allegedly asking for a ceasefire "false and baseless".
Around 180,000 families displaced in Iran, says humanitarian agency
Around 180,000 Iranian families have been displaced due to the ongoing war, although there are no precise figures.
It’s hard to determine exact numbers because Iran doesn’t have a displacement tracking level, according to the International Organization for Migration.
Amy Pope, IOM’s director general, said the agency expects numbers to increase as more civilian infrastructure gets caught in the crossfire. She also warned about the impact on migrants working in Iran who might not be guaranteed the same safety that an Iranian family is seeking.
“This is the kind of hidden consequence of a conflict like this. There are people ... who are not necessarily accounted for and ... won’t have the support they need,” she said.
Pakistani oil tanker transits Strait of Hormuz
A Pakistani oil tanker arrived in Karachi after transiting the Strait of Hormuz, while a second vessel reached the port via a different route.
Karachi Port Trust spokesperson Shariq Farooqi said more Pakistani-flagged ships are expected this month to deliver much-needed oil from Gulf countries.
The development comes days after Pakistan’s foreign minister said Iran had agreed to allow 20 additional Pakistani-flagged ships to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, describing the move as a “constructive gesture” aimed at easing regional tensions.
Trump says Iran president wants ceasefire ahead of his speech to Americans
Donald Trump claims Iran’s president wanted a ceasefire ahead of his speech to the American people.
The US president made the claim on his Truth Social website. Trump said “Iran’s New Regime President,” however Iran still has the same president.
Trump also said a ceasefire would only happen when the Strait of Hormuz is “open, free, clear.”
“Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!” he wrote. Iran had no immediate response to Trump’s post. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in an interview with Al Jazeera aired late Tuesday signaled Tehran’s willingness to keep fighting.
“You cannot speak to the people of Iran in the language of threats and deadlines,” he said. “We do not set any deadline for defending ourselves.”
Energy chief warns of jet fuel and diesel shortages in Europe
Fatih Birol, the head of the International Energy Agency (IEA), has warned of "major disruption" amid the ongoing Middle East conflict, adding that shortages of jet fuel and diesel will soon hit Europe.
"April will be much worse than March", Birol told the In Good Company podcast. This is because oil and gas cargoes that were loaded before the war erupted will still be arriving at ports around the world
"In April, there is nothing," he adds, estimating that the loss of oil to be "twice the loss of oil in March". Birol adds: "we are seeing [the shortages] already in Asia", but this will "soon" be felt in Europe.
Iranian humanitarian worker killed in Iran
A volunteer with the Iranian Red Crescent was killed by an airstrike today in the country’s northwest, according to the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
Alireza Sohbatlou was providing services at a clinic in Zanjan province when an airstrike hit the nearby religious site Azam Hussainiya of Zanjan, the humanitarian network said Wednesday.
He was the third Red Crescent volunteer killed in Iran since the start of the war, the IFRC said.
Reeves says she is 'angry' that Trump went to war with Iran
Rachel Reeves says she is "angry" that Donald Trump went to war in the Middle East.
Speaking on BBC Radio 2's Jeremy Vine show, the Chancellor, who is grappling with impacts of the conflict at home, said: "I'm angry that Donald Trump has chosen to go to war in the Middle East - a war that there's not a clear plan of how to get out of it.
"It's why we didn't want to enter this. Yes it will have implications for our economy, I get that. We are monitoring very closely what's happening - trying to bring the oil and gas into the UK so that those supplies are there and get the prices down. We are monitoring the situation very carefully."
"We are preparing - as you would expect me to be - for every single eventuality to make sure there alongside people, standing beside them, keeping costs down for everyone."
Iran's supreme leader vows to keep backing anti-Israeli forces in message to Hezbollah
Iran’s supreme leader has vowed the country will continue to support anti-Israeli forces in the Middle East.
The message from Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, like others since he was named Iran’s new supreme leader, came in a statement read on air by a state television anchor.
“I firmly declare that the consistent policy of the Islamic Republic of Iran, in continuing the path of the late Imam and martyred leader, is based on continuing to support the resistance against the Zionist-American enemy,” Khamenei said in the comments from a letter to the Lebanese group Hezbollah.
Khamenei has not been seen since the war began on February 28. US and Israeli officials believe he was wounded and remains in hiding.
Russian embassy in Iran condemns missile attack hitting cathedral
The Russian embassy in Iran has condemned an airstrike on the compound of the former US embassy there as it damaged a nearby cathedral.
The embassy said the blast broke doors and windows at St Nicholas Orthodox Cathedral, just across from the compound.
An adjacent Russian nursing home sustained damage, including a collapsed roof, it added. “We strongly condemn the ongoing US and Israeli aggression against Iran, which is increasingly affecting civilian infrastructure and religious and cultural heritage,” the embassy said.
Protester claims oil companies will make 'massive' profits from conflict
Another activist outside the US embassy claims oil bosses are "profitting massively" from the Middle East crisis.
Rosie, 28, who declined to give her surname, said: "We're outside the US embassy because Trump's illegal war on Iran has led to massive spikes in the cost of our energy here in the UK.
"As oil bosses profit massively (...) worse still Trump and Nigel Farage are using this crisis that they fuelled and started as an excuse to drill for more fossil fuels. We're out here to say that for as long as we stay hooked on fossil fuels here in the UK, we are subject of these massive fluctuations in the energy market and true energy security does not mean we should drill for more oil and gas.
"It means that we should harness the power of the wind all around us on this island, the waves and the sun, because we don't fight imperial violent wars to get energy from the sun. It's all around us."
Israel says Hezbollah's Southern Front Commander in Lebanon killed
Hezbollah's Southern Front Commander Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem in Lebanon was killed yesterday, claims the Israeli military.
An IDF spokesperson claimed the Southern Front is carried out attacks in Israel and soldiers in Lebanon, while Hashem was described as "a commander with over 40 years of experience and one of the pillars of the terror organization."
ELIMINATED: Hajj Yusuf Ismail Hashem, the Commander of Hezbollah’s Southern Front
— Israel Defense Forces (@IDF) April 1, 2026
Hashem, eliminated by the Israeli Navy in a strike in Beirut, was a senior commander with 40+ years of experience, and was a central figure in Hezbollah that led its rehabilitation & commanded… pic.twitter.com/a22iexG7pH
Oil protester outside US embassy blasts Trump for rising energy prices
An oil protester outside the US Embassy in London says British people are paying the price for Donald Trump's war in the Middle East.
Fossil Free London activist Robin Wells, 33, told the Mirror: "Donald Trump's foreign interventions are affecting the supply of global oil - it's driving up prices.
"Consumers in the UK have already faced terrible consequences over the last few years... huge energy bills, it's among the top problems faced by the British public and this is only going to get worse if we're locked into fossil fuels.
"So our demonstration today says we shouldn't be tied into oil and gas. It's a nightmare for us, we need to break free of this straight-jacket of oil and gas and into the renewables of the future."
Robin, from Surrey, added: "We're here because Trump is putting a great deal of pressure on the UK to drill for more oil and gas in our declining basin in the North Sea. He's standing against wind power and the far right are following him here.
We're saying that fossil fuels will always lock us into instability, they'll always lock us into crisis, they'll always lock us into more oil wars and big bucks for the bosses. What we need to do is invest in homegrown renewables to safeguard ourselves and prevent the collapse of our food systems and weather systems too.
UK to pursue closer partnership with EU following oil crisis, says Starmer
Britain will pursue a closer security and economic partnership with the European Union in light of the Iran oil crisis, Sir Keir Starmer said.
Speaking at a No 10 press conference, the Prime Minister said: “We will continue to stand up for the British national interest, and we will continue to do what we must to guide our country calmly through this storm.
"However, it is increasingly clear that as the world continues down this volatile path, our long-term national interest requires closer partnership with our allies in Europe and with the European Union.”
Starmer: 'I’m not going to change my position on the war'
Sir Keir Starmer insisted he would not change his position on Britain’s involvement with the war against Iran.
Asked how seriously he took the threat from Donald Trump that the US may no longer come to the UK’s aid in future, he replied: “It is very important that we are clear there’s been a good deal of pressure on me to change my position in relation to joining the war, and I’m not going to change my position on the war.
“So whatever the pressure, whatever the noise, I’m the British Prime Minister, and I have to act in our national interests. I should say that on defence, and security, and intelligence, we are obviously working closely with the US, as we always do. And in relation to the planning on the Strait of Hormuz, of course that involves talking to the Americans as well.
“So as I say, whatever the pressure, whatever the noise, my job is – as British Prime Minister – to concentrate on what’s in the British national interest. That is what’s guided me through this conflict so far. It will continue to guide me as we go forward.”
Starmer says he will act in UK interest 'whatever the noise' after Trump blast
Sir Keir Starmer responded to Donald Trump's criticism by saying he would continue to act in the national interest “whatever the noise”.
He defended NATO as “the single most effective military alliance the world has ever seen” after Trump said he was considering pulling the US out of the bloc.
Trump blasts Starmer and claims UK 'doesn't even have a navy'
Donald Trump attacked Sir Keir Starmer and claimed the Royal Navy is not ready.
He said: “You don’t even have a navy. You’re too old and had aircraft carriers that didn’t work.”
Asked if the UK should spend more on defence, Mr Trump said: “I’m not going to tell him what to do. He can do whatever he wants. It doesn’t matter. All Starmer wants is costly windmills that are driving your energy prices through the roof.”
Donald Trump calls NATO a 'paper tiger' as he considers leaving
Donald Trump has warned that he could pull the US out of NATO.
Speaking to The Telegraph, Trump said the alliance is a “paper tiger” as he said removing the United States from the defence treaty was now “beyond reconsideration”.
Asked if he would reconsider the US’s membership of the alliance after the conflict, Trump: “Oh yes, I would say [it’s] beyond reconsideration. I was never swayed by NATO. I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way.”
PM says impact of Middle East conflict 'will not be easy' for country
The Prime Minister says that the impact of the conflict "will not be easy" for the country.
He has spoken with business leaders, and their concern was not about insurance, but one of safety and security.
Keir Starmer says he understands people are concerned about bills and the price of petrol.
And he say the future partnership with Europe and the European Union is important.
Starmer says UK seeking 'diplomatic route' to reopen Strait of Hormuz
Sir Keir Starmer says the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz is "vital for energy" and that the UK is looking at "each and every diplomatic route available to us" to resolve this.
He stated in the press conference that there are now 38 nations pushing "for maritime safety across the Gulf". And the foreign secretary will host a meeting of the group which will look at all vilable "diplomatic and political" measures.
And he added that the UK is also looking at capabilities to martial the strait is safe after the conflict has stopped.
Starmer starts press conference on Middle East crisis
After a brief delay with journalists getting into the press conference, the press conference has just started with Sir Keir Starmer saying the Iran conflict is "not our war".
And the best way to ease price rises in the UK is seeking "de-escalation".
Huge plumes of smoke coming from Brit oil company in Iraq
Massive plumes of smoke appear to be coming from a British motor oil company hit by drones in Iraq.
Fire can be seen raging from the plant which is in the city of Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region, says a post from Rudaw English.
This morning, two drones struck a British motor oil company in Erbil, causing a massive fire, with no casualties reported - Rudaw's @dilnyarahman reports pic.twitter.com/VLfiCGASz9
— Rudaw English (@RudawEnglish) April 1, 2026
Oil protesters gathers outside US embassy in London over Middle East crisis
Oil protesters have descended on the US embassy in London to demonstrate over America's war on Iran sparking an oil crisis.
Activists from campaign group Fossil Free London began gathering outside the heavily-guarded building in Nine Elms shortly after 8.15am.
Two protesters, with painted white faces, posed next to a yellow mock petrol pump while fake oil was poured on their heads.
Others posed with homemade signs with messages including “Stop Trump” and “Break free from oil wars”.
Others included: “Break free from Rosebank.” The protest comes as the deepening Middle East crisis causes oil prices to surge and analysts warn of jet fuel shortages in Europe within days.
Qatar oil tanker hit by Iranian cruise missile
A Qatari oil tanker has been hit by an Iranian cruise missile while two others were intercepted.
The missile slammed into the tanker which is contracted by state-owned QatarEnergy. The ministry said the tanker’s 21-member crew was evacuated, and no casualties were reported.
In a statement, the Defence Ministry said two other missiles were intercepted. QatarEnergy said there was no environmental impact from the tanker attack.
The British military’s United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center said earlier that a projectile slammed into the side of the ship.
Iran's foreign minister says contact with US but 'no negotiations'
Iran’s foreign minister says he has received direct messages from the US Mideast envoy Steve Witkoff.
Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera that while there had been contact this did not mean they were negotiations.
Donald Trump has repeatedly described Iran and America as having talks over the war, while Pakistan has been a key intermediary along with Egypt and Turkey during the conflict.
“I receive messages from Witkoff directly, as before, and this does not mean that we are in negotiations,” he said. “We do not have any faith that negotiations with the US will yield any results. The trust level is at zero.”

sources.news_title: Trump: Iran Has Asked the Us for a Ceasefire
sources.text:
Der Iran hat die USA gerade um eine Waffenruhe gebeten – das behauptet zumindest Donald Trump. Der US-Präsident knüpft eine mögliche Waffenruhe allerdings an eine Bedingung und „bis dahin bomben wir den Iran in die Vergessenheit.“ Der Iran widerspricht Trumps Aussagen, auch Russland hat sich nun eingeschaltet.
Über eine Waffenruhe werde man nachdenken, „sobald die Straße von Hormuz wieder offen, frei und sicher ist“, erklärte Präsident Trump auf seiner Plattform Truth Social. Bis dahin werde man den Iran in die Vergessenheit bomben, „oder, wie man so schön sagt, zurück in die Steinzeit schicken!!!“
Man habe die USA nicht um eine Waffenruhe gebeten, widerspricht das staatliche iranische Fernsehen unter Berufung auf einen Sprecher des Außenministeriums. Die Aussagen des US-Präsidenten seien falsch und unbegründet.
„Gezielte Schläge“
Die USA würden „ziemlich schnell aus dem Iran abziehen“, sagt Trump in einem Interview der Nachrichtenagentur Reuters. Man könne aber für „gezielte Schläge“ zurückkehren, falls dies nötig sei. Mit den US-Militäraktionen habe man sichergestellt, dass der Iran keine Atomwaffen haben werde, „weil sie dazu jetzt nicht in der Lage sind“, erklärte Trump.
US-Präsident Donald Trump hatte zuvor ein baldiges Ende der Angriffe der US-Armee im Iran in Aussicht gestellt. Er denke, sein Land werde noch „vielleicht zwei Wochen, vielleicht ein paar Tage länger“ brauchen, sagte er am Dienstag im Weißen Haus.
Für eine Öffnung der Straße von Hormuz sieht Trump andere Länder in der Verantwortung. Die USA hätten mit der Sicherung der vom Iran blockierten Meerenge „nichts zu tun“, meinte Trump. Die Straße von Hormuz ist eine der wichtigsten Seefahrtsrouten weltweit und seit Kriegsbeginn praktisch blockiert. Die Meerenge ist für den Transport von Öl und Gas extrem wichtig.
Trump gibt „wichtige“ Rede
Für Mittwoch (Ortszeit) kündigte der US-Präsident eine „wichtige“ Rede zum Stand des Iran-Krieges an. Trump werde am Mittwoch um 21 Uhr Ortszeit (3 Uhr MESZ am Donnerstag) in einer Rede an die Nation ein „wichtiges Update“ zum Iran geben, teilte seine Sprecherin Karoline Leavitt mit.
Verhandlungen in Moskau?
Die russische Nachrichtenagentur TASS meldete unterdessen unter Berufung auf den iranischen Botschafter in Moskau, Kazem Jalali, der Iran würde es begrüßen, wenn Russland in dem Krieg mit den USA und Israel vermitteln würde. Moskau stünde als Mediator bereit, „wenn jeder das will“, reagierte der russische Außenminister Sergej Lawrow.

sources.news_title: Trump says Iran's new leader wants ceasefire
sources.text:
(The Center Square) – President Donald Trump announced today that Iran's new leader has requested a ceasefire, marking a possible turning point in the ongoing conflict that has gripped the region for weeks.
As the U.S.-Iran conflict stretches into its second month following the February 28 attacks, President Trump claims Iran’s new leadership has now requested a ceasefire. This development signals a potential shift in the ongoing hostilities, which have rattled global energy markets and strained American consumers.
The U.S., however, remains firm: any move toward peace hinges on Iran reopening the vital Strait of Hormuz, a flashpoint whose closure has driven oil and gas prices sharply higher.
Trump stated he would only consider Iran's ceasefire proposal if the country reopens the critical Strait of Hormuz, a vital shipping lane for global oil exports.
"Iran's New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a CEASEFIRE!" Trump wrote in a social media post Wednesday morning. "We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear. Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!"
On Tuesday, Trump estimated that the U.S. military campaign against Iran could continue for weeks.
"We're finishing the job, and I think within maybe two weeks, maybe a couple of days longer, to do the job," the president said.
Earlier in the week, Trump struck a different tone, urging U.S. allies to become more involved in the conflict with Iran.
Trump noted that the U.S. does not rely on the Strait of Hormuz for its own oil supply. However, Iran's closure of the waterway occurred after U.S. and Israeli attacks Feb. 28 and has driven up global gas and diesel prices. These price spikes have been felt in the U.S., causing widespread frustration among American consumers.
Since the start of the conflict at the end of February, U.S. gas prices have climbed about $1 per gallon, with the national average recently hitting $4 per gallon.
The ongoing conflict with Iran has rattled global markets, sending oil prices to their highest levels in years. If hostilities continue, experts warn that economic strain will deepen, further burdening U.S. taxpayers.
With U.S. military operations costing more than $1 billion per day, analysts say a prolonged war could drive a significant increase in defense spending and further impact the federal budget. The Department of War has suggested it could request an additional $200 billion from Congress for the Iran operations.
The U.S. and Israel launched attacks on Iran on Feb. 28 after nuclear talks with the Islamic Republic failed to produce a deal. Trump and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth have laid out four military objectives: Destroying Iran's missile capabilities, neutralizing its navy, preventing the development of nuclear weapons, and ensuring the regime can't direct terrorism beyond its borders. Trump and Hegseth have said most of those objectives have been accomplished.

sources.news_title: Donald Trump claims Iran has asked for ceasefire
sources.text:
Iran’s new leadership has asked the US for ceasefire, Donald Trump has claimed.
The US President said he is considering the proposal but that his forces would continue “blasting Iran into oblivion” until the Strait of Hormuz reopens.
In a post on his Truth Social platform on Wednesday, Trump wrote: "Iran's New Regime President, much less Radicalized and far more intelligent than his predecessors, has just asked the United States of America for a ceasefire!
“We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear. Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!! President DJT.”
Iran's foreign ministry rejected Trump's claim as "false and baseless".
Iranian state TV reported the remarks as having been said by foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei.
It comes ahead of Trump’s plan to give an “important update on Iran” in a national address at 9pm EDT on Wednesday (2am BST on Thursday).
The President signalled he will end his war with Iran “soon” - even if Tehran fails to agree to a deal.
“We’ll be leaving very soon,” he told reporters at the White House on Tuesday night, adding that the exit could take place “within two weeks, maybe two weeks, maybe three.”
Asked if successful diplomacy was a prerequisite for the US to end what it calls Operation Epic Fury, Mr Trump said it was not.
“Iran doesn’t have to make a deal, no,” he said.
The comments triggered a fall in the price of oil, with a barrel of Brent Crude dropping from $119 to below $104 in 45 minutes.
Washington had previously threatened to intensify operations if Tehran did not accept a 15-point US ceasefire framework that had among its core demands that Iran commit not to pursue nuclear weapons, halt all uranium enrichment and fully reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump on Wednesday also revealed that he is strongly considering pulling the United States after the conflict in the Middle East.
Read More
The US President described the military alliance as a “paper tiger” and said he had long held doubts about its credibility.
“Oh yes, I would say [it’s] beyond reconsideration,” he told the Telegraph when asked whether he would reconsider the US’s Nato membership after the Middle East conflict.
“I was never swayed by Nato. I always knew they were a paper tiger, and Putin knows that too, by the way.”
In a press conference this morning, Sir Keir Starmer dismissed the comments as “noise”.
The Prime Minister said he would act in the British national interest “whatever the pressure on me and others, whatever the noise” as he vowed the UK would pursue closer ties with European nations.
Asked about Trump’s remarks on the transatlantic military alliance, Sir Keir said: “Firstly, Nato is the single most effective military alliance the world has ever seen, and it has kept us safe for many decades, and we are fully committed to Nato.
“Secondly, that whatever the pressure on me and others, whatever the noise, I'm going to act in the British national interest in all the decisions that I make.
“And that's why I've been absolutely clear that this is not our war and we're not going to get dragged into it.
“But I'm equally clear that, when it comes to defence and security and our economic future, we have to have closer ties with Europe. That's why we had the summit last year.
“This year, as I've just announced, there'll be a further summit. There, we will make good on equipment that we put in place last year, but we will also go further in relation to the alignment.”

sources.text:
President Donald Trump said Wednesday that Iran’s new leadership has asked the United States for a ceasefire.
In a Truth Social post, Trump stated the request came from Iran’s “New Regime President.” Trump said the new president was “less radicalized” and “more intelligent” than his predecessors.
“We will consider when Hormuz Strait is open, free, and clear,” Trump wrote. “Until then, we are blasting Iran into oblivion or, as they say, back to the Stone Ages!!!”
BYRON YORK: TRUMP NEEDS A SHORT WAR
It is not clear who the new “regime president” of Iran is, and Trump did not specify further in his statement.
However, shortly after Trump’s announcement, Iran’s Foreign Minister Araghchi publicly denied that a ceasefire request had been made, telling the Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting news agency that the war will “continue until the aggressor is punished and full compensation is paid to Iran.”
Araghchi also said previous reporting over a five-point proposal from Iran to the U.S. to end the war was “speculation.”
The Strait of Hormuz is a key maritime channel through which about 20% of the world’s oil and gas supplies are shipped. Iran’s closure of the strait has led to a steep increase in the cost of oil, leading to a spike in the price of gas, which hit a national average of $4 a gallon on Tuesday.
Trump waved off the rise in gas prices when asked by reporters, saying that they would come down when the U.S. military operations against Iran end.
“All I have to do is leave Iran, and we’ll be doing that very soon, and they’ll come tumbling down,” Trump said.
The president projected Tuesday that the war against Iran would be over “within maybe two weeks, maybe a couple of days longer to do the job.”
He has repeatedly insisted that Iranian negotiators want to make a deal to end the war and that they allowed oil ships through the Strait of Hormuz last week to show they are “real and solid,” despite public posturing from Iranian officials that no negotiations are taking place.

“Well, I guess they were right, and they were, they were real, and I think they were Pakistani-flagged,” Trump said. “And I said, ‘Well, I guess we’re dealing with the right people.’
